content: The Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) acknowledges the contributions of various organizations and companies in revising the VSP 2018 Construction Guidelines. These guidelines provide detailed instructions for plan reviews, consultations, and construction inspections. When a plan review or construction inspection is requested, VSP evaluates the current construction billing invoices of the shipyard or owner making the request. If invoices are found to be unpaid for more than 90 days, no inspection will be scheduled. Inspections can only proceed once all outstanding invoices are fully paid. The VSP 2018 Construction Guidelines establish consistent construction and design standards to safeguard the health of passengers and crew. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is dedicated to promoting high construction standards to protect public health. Adherence to these guidelines ensures a healthy environment aboard cruise vessels. The CDC developed these guidelines by reviewing references from numerous sources. The guidelines address public health-related components of a vessel’s facilities, including food storage, preparation, and service, as well as water bunkering, storage, disinfection, and distribution. Vessel owners and operators may choose designs and equipment that meet their needs, provided they comply with the sanitary design criteria of the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) or equivalent organizations, as well as VSP’s operational inspection requirements. These guidelines do not restrict the introduction of new designs, materials, or technologies in shipbuilding. Shipbuilders, owners, manufacturers, or other interested parties may request VSP to periodically review or revise the guidelines in light of new information or technology. The guidelines incorporate requirements from international maritime conventions, such as the Safety of Life at Sea Convention, the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships, the Tonnage and Load Line Convention, the International Electrical Code, and the International Plumbing Code. However, the document does not cross-reference related or overlapping standards that new cruise vessels must meet. The VSP 2018 Construction Guidelines became effective on June 1, 2018, and apply to all areas of a vessel affected by renovations after this date. Minor renovations, such as the installation or removal of single pieces of equipment or single pipe runs, are excluded. VSP inspects the entire vessel during routine sanitation inspections and reinspections in accordance with the VSP 2018 Operations Manual. VSP periodically reviews and revises these recommendations in collaboration with industry representatives and other stakeholders to keep pace with industry innovations. Shipbuilders, owners, manufacturers, or other interested parties may request VSP to review a construction guideline based on new technologies, concepts, or methods. Requests should identify the section to be revised, describe the proposed change or addition, state the reason for the recommendation, and include supporting research or test results. VSP coordinates professional evaluations and consults with the industry to determine whether to include the recommendation in the next revision. Special consideration is given to shipyards and vessel owners who have had plan reviews conducted before the effective date of a guideline revision, minimizing the burden of making excessive changes to previously agreed-upon plans. VSP encourages industry representatives and other knowledgeable parties to meet periodically with VSP representatives to review the guidelines and determine whether changes are necessary to keep up with industry innovations. Proposed clarifications to the guidelines, along with supporting information on their public health significance, are circulated in advance of the annual meeting. These clarifications are considered during the meeting. Requests requiring foreign travel must be submitted in writing at least 45 days before the intended visit and will be honored based on VSP staff availability. After initial contact, VSP assigns primary and secondary officers to coordinate with the vessel owner and shipyard. These officers serve as points of contact throughout the plan review, consultations, and final construction inspection. Vessel representatives should also provide points of contact to represent the owners, shipyard, and key subcontractors. All parties use these points of contact to ensure awareness of all consultative activities after the plan review is conducted. VSP typically conducts plan reviews for new construction at least several months before the vessel is scheduled for delivery. The time required for major renovations varies, and VSP coordinates plan reviews well before work begins to allow time for necessary changes. Plan reviews usually take two working days and are conducted in Atlanta, Georgia; Fort Lauderdale, Florida; or other agreed-upon locations. Two VSP officers are typically assigned to the project. Representatives from the shipyard, vessel owner, and subcontractors performing most of the work should attend the review and bring all relevant materials, including complete plans or drawings, menus, equipment specifications, general arrangement plans, decorative materials for food areas and bars, and plans for food-related storage, preparation, and service areas. VSP prepares a plan review report summarizing recommendations made during the review and submits it to the shipyard and owner representatives. Following the review, the shipyard provides redrawn plans and copies of any major change orders made in areas covered by the guidelines. During construction, shipyard representatives, the ship owner, or other vessel representatives may direct questions or requests for consultative services to the VSP project officers. These inquiries should be submitted in writing and include fax numbers and email addresses for appropriate contacts. VSP officers coordinate the request with the owner and shipyard points of contact designated during the plan review. VSP conducts most onsite or shipyard construction inspections outside the United States. Shipyards are encouraged to contact the VSP Chief well in advance of the 45-day minimum to better plan inspection dates. If a shipyard requests an onsite construction inspection, VSP advises the vessel owner of the inspection dates so that the owner’s representatives can be present. Onsite inspections typically require one to three officers, depending on the vessel’s size and whether it is the first of a hull design class or a subsequent hull in the same class. Inspections, including travel, generally take five working days and should be conducted approximately four to five weeks before vessel delivery when 90% of the areas to be inspected are completed. VSP provides a written report to the requesting party. After the inspection and before the ship’s arrival in the United States, the shipyard submits a statement of corrective action to VSP, outlining how it will address and correct each item identified in the inspection report. At the request of a vessel owner or shipyard, VSP may conduct a final construction inspection. These inspections are conducted only after construction is 100% complete and the ship is fully operational. The purpose is to evaluate findings from the previous yard inspection, assess incomplete areas, and test systems that could not be tested earlier. These systems include ventilation for cooking and warewashing areas, warewash machines, artificial light levels, coldor hot-holding equipment temperatures, and halogen or other chemistry measures for potable or recreational water systems. To schedule the inspection, the vessel owner or shipyard submits a formal written request to the VSP Chief as soon as possible after the vessel is completed or at least 10 days before its arrival in the United States. After the final inspection, the vessel owner or shipyard submits a statement of corrective action to VSP, detailing how it will address each item cited in the inspection report and providing a projected completion date. VSP generally schedules vessels that undergo final construction inspections in the United States for an unannounced operational inspection within four weeks of the final construction inspection. If a final construction inspection is not requested, VSP conducts an unannounced operational inspection within four weeks of the vessel’s arrival in the United States. These inspections are conducted in accordance with the VSP 2018 Operations Manual. Although the guidelines establish standards for equipment and materials installed on cruise vessels, VSP does not test, certify, endorse, or approve any equipment or materials used by the cruise industry. Instead, VSP recognizes certification from independent testing laboratories such as NSF International, Underwriters Laboratories (UL), the American National Standards Institute (ANSI), and other recognized independent international testing institutions. Equipment built to questionable standards is reviewed by a committee comprising VSP, cruise ship industry representatives, and independent testing organizations. The committee determines whether the equipment meets the recommended standards established in the guidelines. Equipment manufacturers and suppliers should not contact VSP to request product approval. The VSP 2018 Construction Guidelines provide definitions to clarify commonly used terminology in the manual. Definitions are organized alphabetically, and terms identified in the text are in capital letters.
